package_info.why_malicious: The 'everything' package is intentionally designed to declare dependencies on every publicly available NPM package in its package.json. This results in the NPM package manager attempting to resolve, download, and install an unmanageable number of packages during installation, causing severe resource exhaustion (disk, memory, network) and denial of service (DoS) for any system or CI/CD pipeline that installs it. The package weaponizes the dependency resolution process to disrupt the NPM ecosystem and break build environments.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package.json declares dependencies on every public NPM package, causing the NPM package manager to recursively resolve, download, and install millions of packages, resulting in resource exhaustion and denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Declaring dependencies on every available NPM package is highly abnormal and serves no legitimate purpose. This behavior is engineered to overwhelm the package manager and system resources, leading to denial of service.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package.json should only declare dependencies that are necessary for the package's functionality. This package abuses the dependency mechanism by including all public packages, intentionally causing harm.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate meta-packages may aggregate a small set of related modules, but no valid package would ever depend on every public NPM package.
key_indicators: package.json dependencies list includes all or nearly all public NPM packages
Dependency tree size is orders of magnitude larger than any legitimate package
Install process triggers massive resource consumption (disk, memory, network)
node_modules directory grows to an abnormally large size after install

attack_chain.action: User or CI/CD system installs the 'everything' package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggers the NPM package manager to resolve and download all public packages.

attack_chain.action: NPM attempts to fetch and install millions of dependencies as specified in package.json.
attack_chain.leads_to: System storage, memory, and network bandwidth are exhausted, causing build failures and denial of service.

behavioral_signatures: package.json with dependencies on an abnormally large number of packages (hundreds, thousands, or more)
Install-time resource exhaustion (disk, memory, network) during dependency resolution
CI/CD build failures or timeouts due to excessive dependency trees
node_modules directory size far exceeding typical package installations
file_indicators: package.json with dependencies field listing thousands or millions of packages
node_modules directory containing an unusually high number of subdirectories after install
network_indicators: Massive number of outbound HTTP(S) requests to the NPM registry during install
Sustained high network traffic to registry.npmjs.org or mirrors during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose package.json declares dependencies on an unusually high number of other packages (e.g., more than 100). Flag and block installation of packages with dependency lists that include all or most public NPM packages. Alert on install-time resource exhaustion, excessive node_modules growth, or a surge in network requests to the NPM registry. Automated systems should reject packages with dependency lists that are orders of magnitude larger than typical meta-packages.
